turns.thought:
Yes — please turn mobile data on. MMS (picture messages) requires an active mobile data connection; with data disabled the messages will just sit and fail.

Two things to do on your phone:

1. **Turn mobile data ON** — go to Settings → Network & internet (or Connections) → Mobile network and switch **Mobile data** on. Once it's on, you should see "Data Enabled" in the status bar.
2. **Change your network mode preference** — your status bar shows **2G**, and 2G generally can't carry picture messages. In Settings → Mobile network → Preferred network mode (or Network mode), select **4G/5G preferred** (or at least 4G/LTE).

After both changes, reboot the device once more, then try sending the photo message again.

One account-side item is already handled: I confirmed line **555-123-2002** is Active with 8.7 GB used of 15 GB, no suspension, no overdue bill (February bill of $150.00 is issued but not yet due until 2025-02-19), and international roaming is now enabled on the line.

If the picture message still fails after mobile data is on and you're on 4G/5G, tell me what the status bar shows then — the next things we'd check are Airplane Mode, the SIM status, and your APN (MMSC) settings.
